The '''1990–91''' season was Real Madrid Club de Fútbol's 89th season in existence and the club's 60th consecutive season in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
In the summertime, Welsh head coach [[John Toshack]] asked for several changes, including the transfers of [[Bernd Schuster]] to local rivals [[Atlético Madrid]] and defender [[Oscar Ruggeri]], together with midfielder [[Rafael Martín Vázquez|Martín Vázquez]], to [[Torino FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1990/05/31/deportes/644104811_850215.html|title=Los jugadores defienden a Ruggeri y no hablan de Schuster|work=El País|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1990/10/10/deportes/655513207_850215.html|title=Schuster became the first player to sign for the Three Big Spanish Clubs|work=El País|author=Jose Miguelez|date=9 October 1990|access-date=2 July 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1990/08/23/deportes/651362404_850215.html|work=El País|date=23 August 1990|access-date=2 July 2020|title=Italia entera reconoce a Martín Vázquez...}}</ref> Meanwhile, President Ramon Mendoza, after a failed bid for Liverpool's [[John Barnes]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1990/05/11/deportes/642376803_850215.html|title=Liverpool's CEO Neil White in negotiations with Barnes|date=24 May 1990|language=es|publisher=elpais.com}}</ref> reinforced the club with [[Gheorghe Hagi]], [[Predrag Spasić]] (after [[Gheorghe Popescu (footballer, born 1967)|Gheorghe Popescu]] rejected an offer from Mendoza)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/04/06/primera/1586181081_893623.html|date=6 April 2020|accessdate=6 April 2022|language=es|publisher=as.com|title=Popescu rejected an offer from Madrid due to "a misunderstanding"}}</ref> and Villaroya. Following a losing streak sinking the team down to the 6th place in the league, Mendoza fired Toshack on 25 November 1990 and appointed club legend [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] as a new head coach. The team clinched the Supercopa de España, defeating [[FC Barcelona]] but the situation in the league was worsened with lost matches against [[Athletic Bilbao]], [[Osasuna]], Atlético Madrid and Barcelona.

During February, forward [[Hugo Sánchez]] suffered his first injury,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1991/01/30/deportes/665190002_850215.html|work=El País|title=Hugo Sánchez out for the first time due to an injury|author=Mabel Galaz|date=2 February 1991|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> and the squad was eliminated in the Copa del Rey round of 16 by Atlético Madrid. Then in March, with a high risk of failing to qualify for next year's European competitions, the team was defeated by Russian side [[FC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]] at the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in the European Cup quarter-finals, shattering the chances of Alfredo Di Stéfano to stay as a coach and he resigned after the elimination. After one game with [[Ramón Grosso]] as an interim manager, the club appointed [[Radomir Antić]] as a new permanent head coach.

Surprisingly, despite the chaotic situation and Hugo Sánchez out for the rest of season since 25 April,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1991/04/26/deportes/672616812_850215.html|title=Hugo Sánchez, had a surgery, Out for 6 Months|work=El País|date=25 April 1991|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> Antic managed the squad to reach the third spot in the league standings and the right to play in the [[1991–92 UEFA Cup]]. His notable successes included matches won against Atlético Madrid and Barcelona in the final rounds of the season.
